newsitem.title: GERMANY: German press slam Waigel efforts on budget gap.
newsitem.headline: German press slam Waigel efforts on budget gap.

text.p: German newspapers on Thursday attacked finance minister Theo Waigel for his failure to have made preparations for the widening gap in German public finances that is threatening the country's EMU entry.
"The billion mark hole...How are we going to fill it, Mr Waigel?" asked the mass circulation "Bild" newspaper in a front-page headline.

Certainly not by seeking an early sale of the remaining state-owned shares in telecom giant Deutsche Telekom, a number of editorials begged, referring to comments by Waigel on Wednesday that such a move was being considered.

"Theo Waigel is behaving like someone who has hit on hard times. After a quick look in the piggy bank, off he rushes to the flea market to sell the first thing of value he can lay his hands on," said the Frankfurter Rundschau.

Government coalition sources said on Wednesday that tax revenues would be nearly 20 billion marks less than expected in 1997, throwing Germany's ability to enter European Monetary Union in 1999 more into doubt.

Further sales of Telekom shares would in the long-run make sense and would be sustainable on the bourse, the business daily Handelsblatt said, but it stressed that moving ahead with new sales now would horrify many existing investors.
"In (last year's) issue prospectus it said quite clearly: The sale of shares owned by the federation is expressly forbidden until December 31, 1999.
The newspaper Die Welt said the problem was that Waigel was acting too late. "He failed to implement a thorough turn-around of state financial policies when it was needed," he said.
In the light of such a failure, his insistence in clinging on to a strict interpretation of the budget deficit criterion for single European currency entry was even more striking, it noted.
